text: About 1,350 volcanoes have erupted in the Holocene, the period since the last ice age
as_written: roughly thirteen hundred and fifty volcanoes
source: Smithsonian Institution Global Volcanism Program, Volcanoes of the World database

text: The Holocene began about 11,700 years ago
as_written: about eleven thousand seven hundred years ago
source: International Commission on Stratigraphy, Holocene epoch definition

text: Between 50 and 70 volcanoes erupt in a typical year
as_written: somewhere between fifty and seventy of them erupt
source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program and Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program

text: The mid-ocean ridge system is roughly 65,000 km long
as_written: roughly sixty five thousand kilometres long
source: NOAA Ocean Exploration, mid-ocean ridge system

text: Roughly three quarters of annual magma output comes from mid-ocean ridges
as_written: Roughly three quarters of all the magma Earth erupts each year
source: NOAA Ocean Exploration and USGS, volcanic output at mid-ocean ridges

text: Lava erupts at around 1,000 degrees Celsius
as_written: around one thousand degrees Celsius
source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, lava temperatures

text: About 800 million people live within 100 km of a volcano that has erupted in the Holocene
as_written: about eight hundred million people live within one hundred kilometres
source: Global Volcano Model and IAVCEI, Brown et al. 2015, Global Volcanic Hazards and Risk, and Freire et al. 2019

text: Mount St Helens in 1980 sent an ash column about 24 km high in about 15 minutes
as_written: twenty four kilometres high in about fifteen minutes
source: USGS Cascades Volcano Observatory, 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens

text: Pyroclastic flows can reach up to 700 km/h and hundreds of degrees Celsius
as_written: up to seven hundred kilometres an hour
source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, pyroclastic flows

text: The Mount St Helens lateral blast flattened forest across about 600 square kilometres
as_written: about six hundred square kilometres
source: USGS Cascades Volcano Observatory, May 18 1980 lateral blast

text: 57 people died in the Mount St Helens eruption
as_written: the death toll was fifty seven
source: USGS Cascades Volcano Observatory

text: Eyjafjallajökull in 2010 caused around 100,000 flight cancellations over eight days
as_written: Around one hundred thousand flights were cancelled in eight days
source: Eurocontrol, April 2010 volcanic ash crisis statistics

text: Hunga Tonga plume reached about 57 km, the highest measured by modern instruments
as_written: about fifty seven kilometres
source: Carr et al. 2022, Geophysical Research Letters, Hunga Tonga plume height from satellite imagery

text: The Hunga Tonga atmospheric pressure wave circled the globe and was recorded on barometers
as_written: sent a pressure wave around the entire planet
source: Matoza et al. 2022, Science, atmospheric waves from the Hunga Tonga eruption

text: Pinatubo released about 20 million tonnes of sulphur dioxide
as_written: about twenty million tonnes of sulphur dioxide
source: USGS Fact Sheet 113-97, The Atmospheric Impact of the 1991 Mount Pinatubo Eruption

text: The Pinatubo aerosol cloud circled the globe in about three weeks
as_written: Within about three weeks, the haze had circled the planet
source: USGS Fact Sheet 113-97 and Self et al., Fire and Mud, 1996

text: Pinatubo cooled the globe by about half a degree Celsius for roughly two years
as_written: the whole world cooled by about half a degree Celsius
source: NASA Earth Observatory and USGS Fact Sheet 113-97

text: Pinatubo lahars kept causing damage for years after 1991
as_written: lahars kept killing and burying towns for years
source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program and PHIVOLCS, Pinatubo post-eruption lahars

text: Tambora erupted in 1815 and 1816 was the year without a summer
as_written: the year without a summer
source: Oppenheimer 2003, Progress in Physical Geography, Climatic, environmental and human consequences of the largest known historic eruption; Smithsonian GVP

text: Tambora cooled the global average by roughly half a degree
as_written: fell by roughly half a degree
source: Oppenheimer 2003, Progress in Physical Geography; Raible et al. 2016, WIREs Climate Change

text: Laki in 1783 erupted for about eight months and produced about 14 cubic kilometres of lava
as_written: around fourteen cubic kilometres of lava
source: Thordarson and Self 1993, Bulletin of Volcanology, The Laki and Grimsvotn eruptions 1783-1785

text: Iceland lost about a fifth of its population after Laki
as_written: Iceland lost about a fifth of its population
source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Laki; Thordarson and Self 2003, Journal of Geophysical Research

text: About 23,000 excess deaths in Britain from the Laki haze
as_written: roughly twenty three thousand extra deaths in Britain
source: Witham and Oppenheimer 2005, Bulletin of Volcanology, Mortality in England during the 1783-4 Laki Craters eruption

text: Toba erupted about 74,000 years ago, and its role in a human population bottleneck is disputed
as_written: About seventy four thousand years ago
source: Smithsonian GVP; Petraglia et al. 2007, Science; Smith et al. 2018, Nature Communications, Toba and human survival in Africa

text: The Siberian Traps erupted about 252 million years ago, coinciding with the end-Permian extinction
as_written: two hundred and fifty two million years ago
source: Burgess, Bowring and Shen 2014, PNAS, High-precision timeline for Earth's most severe extinction

text: The end-Permian extinction wiped out the great majority of marine species
as_written: the great majority of marine species vanished
source: Stanley 2016, PNAS, Estimates of the magnitudes of major marine mass extinctions; Burgess et al. 2017, Nature Communications

text: Humans emit 60 to 100 times more CO2 each year than all volcanoes combined
as_written: sixty to one hundred times more carbon dioxide
source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, Volcanoes Can Affect Climate; Gerlach 2011, Eos

text: Hunga Tonga injected about 146 million tonnes of water into the stratosphere, about 10 percent of its water content
as_written: about one hundred and forty six million tonnes of water
source: Millán et al. 2022, Geophysical Research Letters, using NASA Aura Microwave Limb Sounder data

text: Hunga Tonga raised stratospheric water by around ten percent
as_written: by around ten percent
source: Millán et al. 2022, Geophysical Research Letters

text: Kasatochi erupted in August 2008 in the Aleutians
as_written: In August of 2008
source: Smithsonian GVP; Waythomas et al. 2010, Journal of Geophysical Research

text: Fraser River sockeye returns in 2010 were the largest in nearly a century, far above forecast, possibly due to iron from Kasatochi ash; the link is debated
as_written: more sockeye salmon came back to the Fraser River in Canada than in almost a century
source: Parsons and Whitney 2012, Fisheries Oceanography; Pacific Salmon Commission 2010 return data

text: Volcanic ash is rich in iron and can fertilise iron-limited ocean regions
as_written: Volcanic ash is rich in iron
source: Langmann et al. 2010, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, Volcanic ash as fertiliser for the surface ocean

text: Volcanic ash weathers into fertile soil
as_written: some of the most fertile soil on Earth
source: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, Andisols soil order
